stories.body: Iran says it is continuing to circumvent a US-imposed blockade affecting its oil industry, describing conditions as difficult but manageable, while Washington says it is keeping all options open, including military pressure. South Korea is considering possible contributions to US-led security efforts to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, although its presidential office says no deployment has been decided. Reports have suggested Seoul could seek parliamentary approval to send assets including a maritime patrol aircraft and logistics ship; the country depends on the strait for much of its energy imports.
stories.headline: Iran conflict raises pressure on Strait of Hormuz shipping as Washington keeps military options open

stories.body: Rescuers have pulled two workers alive from a mud- and debris-blocked tunnel at Nepal's Trishuli 3A hydropower station, nine days after devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border. Engineers used old maps, satellite images and surface clues to locate the tunnel entrance after an avalanche buried it, then drained water, cleared debris including with carefully controlled explosives, and dug a narrow passage. The two men were taken to hospital with injuries, one reported in critical condition, while rescuers believe more people may remain trapped in tunnels linked to hydropower projects across the affected Himalayan region.
stories.headline: Two hydropower workers rescued from Nepal tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods

stories.body: The World Meteorological Organization says the developing El Niño is likely to become very strong, could be the strongest in decades and is expected to persist until at least February 2027. The phenomenon is already pushing tropical Pacific sea-surface temperatures sharply above average and could intensify droughts, floods, typhoons and extreme heat in different regions, on top of human-driven warming. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that the world had entered a danger zone of extreme weather, while the WMO called for early-warning systems and preventive measures to protect communities, food production and economies.
stories.headline: UN warns a potentially supersized El Niño could bring severe global economic and weather impacts

stories.body: Volkswagen's supervisory board has approved a further 50,000 job cuts by 2030, bringing planned reductions across the group to 100,000, or roughly 15% of its workforce. The company will also halve the number of models it produces, reduce product complexity by 75%, and assess alternative uses for four German plants where capacity exceeds demand. Volkswagen says falling sales, US import tariffs, overcapacity and increasingly competitive Chinese manufacturers have forced the restructuring, though investors welcomed the approval as evidence that its governance structure can carry out major reforms.
stories.headline: Volkswagen approves restructuring plan with 50,000 further job cuts amid tariffs, overcapacity and Chinese competition

stories.body: Nvidia has agreed to acquire the AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, extending its reach in open-source artificial intelligence. The deal would bring Nvidia closer to the developers using and building AI models and broaden its customer base as major technology companies develop their own chips to reduce dependence on Nvidia.
stories.headline: Nvidia agrees to buy AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion

stories.body: Missouri's Supreme Court has unanimously suspended a Republican-drawn congressional map until voters decide its fate in a November referendum. The court ruled that the Democratic-backed referendum petition challenging the map was wrongly declared insufficient, meaning the state's 2022 districts will remain in force for the general election. The decision is likely to preserve a Kansas City-based House seat held by Democrat Emanuel Cleaver, despite primaries having already been conducted under the newer map; the state attorney general says she will ask the US Supreme Court to intervene.
stories.headline: Missouri Supreme Court blocks Republican congressional map for the November midterms

stories.body: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to allow its restrictions on mail-in ballots to take effect ahead of November's midterm elections. The request follows a fast-moving legal battle over whether the measures can be implemented in time for the election.
stories.headline: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to permit restrictions on mail-in ballots before the midterms

stories.body: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's latest effort to limit birthright citizenship, ruling that the legal question raised by the president's August executive order had already been settled by the Supreme Court. The judge said that no presidential executive order could undo what the court had established.
stories.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump's latest attempt to limit birthright citizenship

stories.body: Federal prosecutors have charged ICE agent Christian Castro with lying to investigators about the January shooting of Venezuelan migrant Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis in Minnesota. Authorities allege Castro fired through the closed door of an occupied home, striking Sosa-Celis in the leg, then falsely claimed he had been attacked; surveillance footage reportedly contradicted that account. Castro also faces state charges including assault and false reporting, and the case is notable because criminal charges against a federal immigration officer by the current Justice Department are rare.
stories.headline: ICE agent charged with lying under oath about a Minnesota shooting

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said Spain will investigate whether Moroccan authorities acted through inaction or incapacity during the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta at the end of July, while maintaining there is not yet proof that Rabat planned the episode. He announced the declassification of intelligence reports from the period, after a police report reportedly indicated that Moroccan agents helped direct migrants toward the border breakwaters. Opposition parties and some government allies have criticized Sánchez's cautious diplomatic approach, while Morocco has continued asserting its territorial claim over Ceuta.
stories.headline: Spain's government hardens its stance on Morocco as the Ceuta migration crisis drives political and legal conflict

stories.body: The European Commission says it has made important progress toward releasing emergency assistance for Ceuta after Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska provided further explanations on Spain's funding request. The aid, reported to exceed €100 million, could support border-protection equipment, migrant accommodation and returns, but Brussels had delayed approval pending clarifications and a formal request. Spain has also shifted toward seeking a more permanent Frontex presence and a specific Europol mission as the city continues to face an unprecedented migration crisis.
stories.headline: EU emergency aid for Ceuta moves closer after Spain provides further information

stories.body: Spain has proposed that the EU create a climate-resilience levy on the profits of oil and gas companies to help finance adaptation to climate change. Its plan calls for a dedicated European climate-adaptation fund, potentially supplemented by charges on private aviation, common EU debt instruments and climate-risk bonds. The government argues that public planning, investment decisions and private investment should systematically account for climate risks under the polluter-pays principle.
stories.headline: Spain proposes an EU levy on oil and gas companies to fund climate action

stories.body: Catalonia's High Court of Justice has applied the partial pardon granted to former Catalan parliament speaker Laura Borràs, reducing her prison sentence from four years, six months and one day to two years. The court has given prosecutors and Borràs's defense 10 days to comment on whether the sentence should be suspended, since it does not exceed two years and is her only prison sentence. Her nine-year-and-one-day disqualification from public office and fine remain in force, and the pardon requires her not to commit an intentional crime for five years.
stories.headline: Catalonia court applies Laura Borràs's partial pardon, opening the way to suspend her prison sentence

stories.body: Ten people were injured by carbon monoxide poisoning aboard the Ocean Euphrosine at Barcelona's Energy Wharf while the vessel was unloading vegetable oils. One man was taken to Hospital Clínic in critical condition and another was hospitalized in serious condition, while several others sustained less serious injuries or were treated at the scene. Emergency services deployed 12 ambulances and firefighters sent nine units; the Civil Guard and maritime authorities are investigating the cause, and port operations were not disrupted.
stories.headline: Ten people suffer carbon monoxide poisoning aboard a ship at the Port of Barcelona, including one in critical condition

stories.body: Catalonia recorded 1,835 heat-related deaths between June and August, according to the Carlos III Health Institute's daily mortality monitoring system, nearly three times the previous high of 669 deaths in 2025. August accounted for 1,164 of the deaths, with a major concentration during the third week of the month. The summer was also Catalonia's warmest on record, while primary care treated 5,771 people for heat effects between May and late August, emergency departments treated more than 2,000, and 361 were hospitalized.
stories.headline: Catalonia records 1,835 heat-related deaths this summer, nearly triple last year's previous high

stories.body: Volkswagen's approved restructuring plan has intensified uncertainty around Seat, although no specific decision on ending the Martorell-based brand was made at the supervisory board meeting. The group has said it does not plan to electrify Seat models, but has left open the possibility that the Martorell factory could receive a second electric-vehicle platform after 2030. Seat's works council says employment is guaranteed through 2030 and argues that a second platform would protect future production, while Catalan President Salvador Illa has pledged government support to preserve the region's automotive industry and jobs.
stories.headline: Volkswagen restructuring puts Seat's future and Catalan jobs in doubt

stories.body: The CGT union says 23% of Catalonia's public-school educational support staff remain without contracts less than a week before the school year begins. The problem mainly affects special-education workers, social-integration technicians and early-childhood specialists whose contracts ended on 31 August, with the union blaming errors in transfer competitions and administrative delays. The dispute comes as USTEC and CGT maintain a strike planned for 8 September after talks with Education Minister Esther Niubó failed to produce a timetable for renewed negotiations.
stories.headline: Education workers say 23% of Catalonia's support staff remain without contracts days before the school year begins
